title: Adjoint kernel on algebra-valued points
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, write $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$, using the affine test schemes and maps of [def-sc-gm-ga], and let $A[\epsilon]$ be the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Let $p:A[\epsilon]\to A$ and $c:A\to A[\epsilon]$ be the augmentation and constant inclusion. Define $K_G(A)=\{g\in G(A): c_*(g)v=vc_*(g)\text{ for every }v\in G(A[\epsilon])\text{ with }p_*(v)=1\}$. Thus $K_G(A)$ consists of points whose conjugation fixes every tangent vector at the identity over $A$. For a smooth finite-type group over a field this is the functor of points of the kernel of the adjoint representation. There is no reducedness assumption on $A$.

source.place: 10.20--10.23, differentiated conjugation, and Proposition 14.23, printed p.285; the identity tangent vectors over A are the kernel of reduction on A[epsilon]-points.
